_about: The Latin Vulgate (Clementine, 1592) and the Douay-Rheims English made from it (Challoner, 1750), public domain, under the Vulgate’s own verse numbers. The Vulgate keeps the Old Latin of Wisdom, which Jerome did not revise.

vulgate.1:1: Diligite justitiam, qui judicatis terram. Sentite de Domino in bonitate, et in simplicitate cordis quærite illum:
vulgate.1:2: quoniam invenitur ab his qui non tentant illum, apparet autem eis qui fidem habent in illum.
vulgate.1:3: Perversæ enim cogitationes separant a Deo; probata autem virtus corripit insipientes.
vulgate.1:4: Quoniam in malevolam animam non introibit sapientia, nec habitabit in corpore subdito peccatis.
vulgate.1:5: Spiritus enim sanctus disciplinæ effugiet fictum, et auferet se a cogitationibus quæ sunt sine intellectu, et corripietur a superveniente iniquitate.
vulgate.1:6: Benignus est enim spiritus sapientiæ, et non liberabit maledicum a labiis suis: quoniam renum illius testis est Deus, et cordis illius scrutator est verus, et linguæ ejus auditor.
vulgate.1:7: Quoniam spiritus Domini replevit orbem terrarum, et hoc quod continet omnia, scientiam habet vocis.
vulgate.1:8: Propter hoc qui loquitur iniqua non potest latere, nec præteriet illum corripiens judicium.
vulgate.1:9: In cogitationibus enim impii interrogatio erit; sermonum autem illius auditio ad Deum veniet, ad correptionem iniquitatum illius.
vulgate.1:10: Quoniam auris zeli audit omnia, et tumultus murmurationum non abscondetur.
vulgate.1:11: Custodite ergo vos a murmuratione quæ nihil prodest, et a detractione parcite linguæ: quoniam sermo obscurus in vacuum non ibit, os autem quod mentitur occidit animam.
vulgate.1:12: Nolite zelare mortem in errore vitæ vestræ, neque acquiratis perditionem in operibus manuum vestrarum.
vulgate.1:13: Quoniam Deus mortem non fecit, nec lætatur in perditione vivorum.
vulgate.1:14: Creavit enim ut essent omnia, et sanabiles fecit nationes orbis terrarum: et non est in illis medicamentum exterminii, nec inferorum regnum in terra.
vulgate.1:15: Justitia enim perpetua est, et immortalis.
vulgate.1:16: Impii autem manibus et verbis accersierunt illam, et æstimantes illam amicam, defluxerunt; et sponsiones posuerunt ad illam, quoniam digni sunt qui sint ex parte illius.
vulgate.2:1: Dixerunt enim cogitantes apud se non recte: Exiguum et cum tædio est tempus vitæ nostræ, et non est refrigerium in fine hominis, et non est qui agnitus sit reversus ab inferis.
vulgate.2:2: Quia ex nihilo nati sumus, et post hoc erimus tamquam non fuerimus. Quoniam fumus flatus est in naribus nostris, et sermo scintilla ad commovendum cor nostrum:
vulgate.2:3: qua extincta, cinis erit corpus nostrum, et spiritus diffundetur tamquam mollis aër; et transibit vita nostra tamquam vestigium nubis, et sicut nebula dissolvetur quæ fugata est a radiis solis, et a calore illius aggravata.
vulgate.2:4: Et nomen nostrum oblivionem accipiet per tempus, et nemo memoriam habebit operum nostrorum.
vulgate.2:5: Umbræ enim transitus est tempus nostrum, et non est reversio finis nostri: quoniam consignata est, et nemo revertitur.
vulgate.2:6: Venite ergo, et fruamur bonis quæ sunt, et utamur creatura tamquam in juventute celeriter.
vulgate.2:7: Vino pretioso et unguentis nos impleamus, et non prætereat nos flos temporis.
vulgate.2:8: Coronemus nos rosis antequam marcescant; nullum pratum sit quod non pertranseat luxuria nostra:
vulgate.2:9: nemo nostrum exsors sit luxuriæ nostræ. Ubique relinquamus signa lætitiæ, quoniam hæc est pars nostra, et hæc est sors.
vulgate.2:10: Opprimamus pauperem justum, et non parcamus viduæ, nec veterani revereamur canos multi temporis:
vulgate.2:11: sit autem fortitudo nostra lex justitiæ; quod enim infirmum est, inutile invenitur.
vulgate.2:12: Circumveniamus ergo justum, quoniam inutilis est nobis, et contrarius est operibus nostris, et improperat nobis peccata legis, et diffamat in nos peccata disciplinæ nostræ.
vulgate.2:13: Promittit se scientiam Dei habere, et filium Dei se nominat.
vulgate.2:14: Factus est nobis in traductionem cogitationum nostrarum.
vulgate.2:15: Gravis est nobis etiam ad videndum, quoniam dissimilis est aliis vita illius, et immutatæ sunt viæ ejus.
vulgate.2:16: Tamquam nugaces æstimati sumus ab illo, et abstinet se a viis nostris tamquam ab immunditiis, et præfert novissima justorum, et gloriatur patrem se habere Deum.
vulgate.2:17: Videamus ergo si sermones illius veri sint, et tentemus quæ ventura sunt illi, et sciemus quæ erunt novissima illius.
vulgate.2:18: Si enim est verus filius Dei, suscipiet illum, et liberabit eum de manibus contrariorum.
vulgate.2:19: Contumelia et tormento interrogemus eum, ut sciamus reverentiam ejus, et probemus patientiam illius.
vulgate.2:20: Morte turpissima condemnemus eum; erit enim ei respectus ex sermonibus illius.
vulgate.2:21: Hæc cogitaverunt, et erraverunt: excæcavit enim illos malitia eorum.
vulgate.2:22: Et nescierunt sacramenta Dei: neque mercedem speraverunt justitiæ, nec judicaverunt honorem animarum sanctarum.
vulgate.2:23: Quoniam Deus creavit hominem inexterminabilem, et ad imaginem similitudinis suæ fecit illum.
vulgate.2:24: Invidia autem diaboli mors introivit in orbem terrarum:
vulgate.2:25: imitantur autem illum qui sunt ex parte illius.
vulgate.3:1: Justorum autem animæ in manu Dei sunt, et non tanget illos tormentum mortis.
vulgate.3:2: Visi sunt oculis insipientium mori, et æstimata est afflictio exitus illorum,
vulgate.3:3: et quod a nobis est iter exterminium; illi autem sunt in pace:
vulgate.3:4: etsi coram hominibus tormenta passi sunt, spes illorum immortalitate plena est.
vulgate.3:5: In paucis vexati sunt, in multis bene disponentur, quoniam Deus tentavit eos, et invenit illos dignos se.
vulgate.3:6: Tamquam aurum in fornace probavit illos, et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit illos, et in tempore erit respectus illorum.
vulgate.3:7: Fulgebunt justi et tamquam scintillæ in arundineto discurrent.
vulgate.3:8: Judicabunt nationes, et dominabuntur populis, et regnabit Dominus illorum in perpetuum.
vulgate.3:9: Qui confidunt in illo intelligent veritatem, et fideles in dilectione acquiescent illi, quoniam donum et pax est electis ejus.
vulgate.3:10: Impii autem secundum quæ cogitaverunt correptionem habebunt: qui neglexerunt justum, et a Domino recesserunt.
vulgate.3:11: Sapientiam enim et disciplinam qui abjicit infelix est: et vacua est spes illorum, et labores sine fructu, et inutilia opera eorum.
vulgate.3:12: Mulieres eorum insensatæ sunt, et nequissimi filii eorum.
vulgate.3:13: Maledicta creatura eorum, quoniam felix est sterilis; et incoinquinata, quæ nescivit thorum in delicto, habebit fructum in respectione animarum sanctarum;
vulgate.3:14: et spado qui non operatus est per manus suas iniquitatem, nec cogitavit adversus Deum nequissima: dabitur enim illi fidei donum electum, et sors in templo Dei acceptissima.
vulgate.3:15: Bonorum enim laborum gloriosus est fructus, et quæ non concidat radix sapientiæ.
vulgate.3:16: Filii autem adulterorum in inconsummatione erunt, et ab iniquo thoro semen exterminabitur.
vulgate.3:17: Et si quidem longæ vitæ erunt, in nihilum computabuntur, et sine honore erit novissima senectus illorum:
vulgate.3:18: et si celerius defuncti fuerint, non habebunt spem, nec in die agnitionis allocutionem.
vulgate.3:19: Nationis enim iniquæ diræ sunt consummationes.
vulgate.4:1: O quam pulchra est casta generatio, cum claritate! immortalis est enim memoria illius, quoniam et apud Deum nota est, et apud homines.
vulgate.4:2: Cum præsens est, imitantur illam, et desiderant eam cum se eduxerit; et in perpetuum coronata triumphat, incoinquinatorum certaminum præmium vincens.
vulgate.4:3: Multigena autem impiorum multitudo non erit utilis, et spuria vitulamina non dabunt radices altas, nec stabile firmamentum collocabunt.
vulgate.4:4: Etsi in ramis in tempore germinaverint, infirmiter posita, a vento commovebuntur, et a nimietate ventorum eradicabuntur.
vulgate.4:5: Confringentur enim rami inconsummati; et fructus illorum inutiles et acerbi ad manducandum, et ad nihilum apti.
vulgate.4:6: Ex iniquis enim somnis filii qui nascuntur, testes sunt nequitiæ adversus parentes in interrogatione sua.
vulgate.4:7: Justus autem si morte præoccupatus fuerit, in refrigerio erit;
vulgate.4:8: senectus enim venerabilis est non diuturna, neque annorum numero computata: cani autem sunt sensus hominis,
vulgate.4:10: Placens Deo factus est dilectus, et vivens inter peccatores translatus est.
vulgate.4:11: Raptus est, ne malitia mutaret intellectum ejus, aut ne fictio deciperet animam illius.
vulgate.4:12: Fascinatio enim nugacitatis obscurat bona, et inconstantia concupiscentiæ transvertit sensum sine malitia.
vulgate.4:13: Consummatus in brevi, explevit tempora multa;
vulgate.4:14: placita enim erat Deo anima illius: propter hoc properavit educere illum de medio iniquitatum. Populi autem videntes, et non intelligentes, nec ponentes in præcordiis talia,
vulgate.4:15: quoniam gratia Dei et misericordia est in sanctos ejus, et respectus in electos illius.
vulgate.4:16: Condemnat autem justus mortuus vivos impios, et juventus celerius consummata longam vitam injusti.
vulgate.4:17: Videbunt enim finem sapientis, et non intelligent quid cogitaverit de illo Deus, et quare munierit illum Dominus.
vulgate.4:18: Videbunt, et contemnent eum; illos autem Dominus irridebit.
vulgate.4:19: Et erunt post hæc decidentes sine honore, et in contumelia inter mortuos in perpetuum: quoniam disrumpet illos inflatos sine voce, et commovebit illos a fundamentis, et usque ad supremum desolabuntur, et erunt gementes, et memoria illorum peribit.
vulgate.4:20: Venient in cogitatione peccatorum suorum timidi, et traducent illos ex adverso iniquitates ipsorum.
vulgate.5:1: Tunc stabunt justi in magna constantia adversus eos qui se angustiaverunt, et qui abstulerunt labores eorum.
vulgate.5:2: Videntes turbabuntur timore horribili, et mirabuntur in subitatione insperatæ salutis;
vulgate.5:3: dicentes intra se, pœnitentiam agentes, et præ angustia spiritus gementes: Hi sunt quos habuimus aliquando in derisum, et in similitudinem improperii.
vulgate.5:4: Nos insensati, vitam illorum æstimabamus insaniam, et finem illorum sine honore;
vulgate.5:5: ecce quomodo computati sunt inter filios Dei, et inter sanctos sors illorum est.
vulgate.5:6: Ergo erravimus a via veritatis, et justitiæ lumen non luxit nobis, et sol intelligentiæ non est ortus nobis.
vulgate.5:7: Lassati sumus in via iniquitatis et perditionis, et ambulavimus vias difficiles: viam autem Domini ignoravimus.
vulgate.5:8: Quid nobis profuit superbia? aut divitiarum jactantia quid contulit nobis?
vulgate.5:9: Transierunt omnia illa tamquam umbra, et tamquam nuntius percurrens,
vulgate.5:10: et tamquam navis quæ pertransit fluctuantem aquam, cujus cum præterierit non est vestigium invenire, neque semitam carinæ illius in fluctibus;
vulgate.5:11: aut tamquam avis quæ transvolat in aëre, cujus nullum invenitur argumentum itineris, sed tantum sonitus alarum verberans levem ventum, et scindens per vim itineris aërem: commotis alis transvolavit, et post hoc nullum signum invenitur itineris illius;
vulgate.5:12: aut tamquam sagitta emissa in locum destinatum, divisus aër continuo in se reclusus est, ut ignoretur transitus illius:
vulgate.5:13: sic et nos nati continuo desivimus esse; et virtutis quidem nullum signum valuimus ostendere, in malignitate autem nostra consumpti sumus.
vulgate.5:14: Talia dixerunt in inferno hi qui peccaverunt:
vulgate.5:15: quoniam spes impii tamquam lanugo est quæ a vento tollitur, et tamquam spuma gracilis quæ a procella dispergitur, et tamquam fumus qui a vento diffusus est, et tamquam memoria hospitis unius diei prætereuntis.
vulgate.5:16: Justi autem in perpetuum vivent, et apud Dominum est merces eorum, et cogitatio illorum apud Altissimum.
vulgate.5:17: Ideo accipient regnum decoris, et diadema speciei de manu Domini: quoniam dextera sua teget eos, et brachio sancto suo defendet illos.
vulgate.5:18: Accipiet armaturam zelus illius, et armabit creaturam ad ultionem inimicorum.
vulgate.5:19: Induet pro thorace justitiam, et accipiet pro galea judicium certum;
vulgate.5:21: Acuet autem duram iram in lanceam, et pugnabit cum illo orbis terrarum contra insensatos.
vulgate.5:22: Ibunt directe emissiones fulgurum, et tamquam a bene curvato arcu nubium exterminabuntur, et ad certum locum insilient.
vulgate.5:23: Et a petrosa ira plenæ mittentur grandines; excandescet in illos aqua maris, et flumina concurrent duriter.
vulgate.5:24: Contra illos stabit spiritus virtutis, et tamquam turbo venti dividet illos; et ad eremum perducet omnem terram iniquitas illorum, et malignitas evertet sedes potentium.
vulgate.6:1: Melior est sapientia quam vires, et vir prudens quam fortis.
vulgate.6:2: Audite ergo, reges, et intelligite; discite, judices finium terræ.
vulgate.6:3: Præbete aures, vos qui continetis multitudines, et placetis vobis in turbis nationum.
vulgate.6:4: Quoniam data est a Domino potestas vobis, et virtus ab Altissimo: qui interrogabit opera vestra, et cogitationes scrutabitur.
vulgate.6:5: Quoniam cum essetis ministri regni illius, non recte judicastis, nec custodistis legem justitiæ, neque secundum voluntatem Dei ambulastis.
vulgate.6:6: Horrende et cito apparebit vobis, quoniam judicium durissimum his qui præsunt fiet.
vulgate.6:7: Exiguo enim conceditur misericordia; potentes autem potenter tormenta patientur.
vulgate.6:8: Non enim subtrahet personam cujusquam Deus, nec verebitur magnitudinem ejus cujusquam, quoniam pusillum et magnum ipse fecit, et æqualiter cura est illi de omnibus.
vulgate.6:10: Ad vos ergo, reges, sunt hi sermones mei: ut discatis sapientiam, et non excidatis.
vulgate.6:11: Qui enim custodierint justa juste, justificabuntur; et qui didicerint ista, invenient quid respondeant.
vulgate.6:12: Concupiscite ergo sermones meos; diligite illos, et habebitis disciplinam.
vulgate.6:13: Clara est, et quæ numquam marcescit, sapientia: et facile videtur ab his qui diligunt eam, et invenitur ab his qui quærunt illam.
vulgate.6:14: Præoccupat qui se concupiscunt, ut illis se prior ostendat.
vulgate.6:15: Qui de luce vigilaverit ad illam non laborabit; assidentem enim illam foribus suis inveniet.
vulgate.6:16: Cogitare ergo de illa sensus est consummatus, et qui vigilaverit propter illam cito securus erit.
vulgate.6:17: Quoniam dignos se ipsa circuit quærens, et in viis ostendit se hilariter, et in omni providentia occurrit illis.
vulgate.6:18: Initium enim illius verissima est disciplinæ concupiscentia.
vulgate.6:19: Cura ergo disciplinæ dilectio est, et dilectio custodia legum illius est; custoditio autem legum consummatio incorruptionis est;
vulgate.6:20: incorruptio autem facit esse proximum Deo.
vulgate.6:21: Concupiscentia itaque sapientiæ deducit ad regnum perpetuum.
vulgate.6:22: Si ergo delectamini sedibus et sceptris, o reges populi, diligite sapientiam, ut in perpetuum regnetis:
vulgate.6:23: diligite lumen sapientiæ, omnes qui præestis populis.
vulgate.6:24: Quid est autem sapientia, et quemadmodum facta sit, referam, et non abscondam a vobis sacramenta Dei: sed ab initio nativitatis investigabo, et ponam in lucem scientiam illius, et non præteribo veritatem.
vulgate.6:25: Neque cum invidia tabescente iter habebo, quoniam talis homo non erit particeps sapientiæ.
vulgate.6:26: Multitudo autem sapientium sanitas est orbis terrarum, et rex sapiens stabilimentum populi est.
vulgate.6:27: Ergo accipite disciplinam per sermones meos, et proderit vobis.
vulgate.7:1: Sum quidem et ego mortalis homo, similis omnibus, et ex genere terreni illius qui prior factus est: et in ventre matris figuratus sum caro;
vulgate.7:2: decem mensium tempore coagulatus sum in sanguine: ex semine hominis, et delectamento somni conveniente.
vulgate.7:3: Et ego natus accepi communem aërem, et in similiter factam decidi terram, et primam vocem similem omnibus emisi plorans.
vulgate.7:4: In involumentis nutritus sum, et curis magnis:
vulgate.7:5: nemo enim ex regibus aliud habuit nativitatis initium.
vulgate.7:6: Unus ergo introitus est omnibus ad vitam, et similis exitus.
vulgate.7:7: Propter hoc optavi, et datus est mihi sensus; et invocavi, et venit in me spiritus sapientiæ:
vulgate.7:8: et præposui illam regnis et sedibus, et divitias nihil esse duxi in comparatione illius.
vulgate.7:9: Nec comparavi illi lapidem pretiosum, quoniam omne aurum in comparatione illius arena est exigua, et tamquam lutum æstimabitur argentum in conspectu illius.
vulgate.7:10: Super salutem et speciem dilexi illam, et proposui pro luce habere illam, quoniam inextinguibile est lumen illius.
vulgate.7:11: Venerunt autem mihi omnia bona pariter cum illa, et innumerabilis honestas per manus illius;
vulgate.7:12: et lætatus sum in omnibus, quoniam antecedebat me ista sapientia, et ignorabam quoniam horum omnium mater est.
vulgate.7:13: Quam sine fictione didici, et sine invidia communico, et honestatem illius non abscondo.
vulgate.7:14: Infinitus enim thesaurus est hominibus; quo qui usi sunt, participes facti sunt amicitiæ Dei, propter disciplinæ dona commendati.
vulgate.7:15: Mihi autem dedit Deus dicere ex sententia, et præsumere digna horum quæ mihi dantur: quoniam ipse sapientiæ dux est, et sapientium emendator.
vulgate.7:16: In manu enim illius et nos et sermones nostri, et omnis sapientia, et operum scientia, et disciplina.
vulgate.7:17: Ipse enim dedit mihi horum quæ sunt scientiam veram, ut sciam dispositionem orbis terrarum, et virtutes elementorum,
vulgate.7:18: initium, et consummationem, et medietatem temporum, vicissitudinum permutationes, et commutationes temporum,
vulgate.7:20: naturas animalium, et iras bestiarum, vim ventorum, et cogitationes hominum, differentias virgultorum, et virtutes radicum.
vulgate.7:21: Et quæcumque sunt absconsa et improvisa didici: omnium enim artifex docuit me sapientia.
vulgate.7:22: Est enim in illa spiritus intelligentiæ, sanctus, unicus, multiplex, subtilis, disertus, mobilis, incoinquinatus, certus, suavis, amans bonum, acutus, quem nihil vetat, benefaciens,
vulgate.7:23: humanus, benignus, stabilis, certus, securus, omnem habens virtutem, omnia prospiciens, et qui capiat omnes spiritus, intelligibilis, mundus, subtilis.
vulgate.7:24: Omnibus enim mobilibus mobilior est sapientia: attingit autem ubique propter suam munditiam.
vulgate.7:25: Vapor est enim virtutis Dei, et emanatio quædam est claritatis omnipotentis Dei sincera, et ideo nihil inquinatum in eam incurrit:
vulgate.7:26: candor est enim lucis æternæ, et speculum sine macula Dei majestatis, et imago bonitatis illius.
vulgate.7:27: Et cum sit una, omnia potest; et in se permanens omnia innovat: et per nationes in animas sanctas se transfert; amicos Dei et prophetas constituit.
vulgate.7:28: Neminem enim diligit Deus, nisi eum qui cum sapientia inhabitat.
vulgate.7:29: Est enim hæc speciosior sole, et super omnem dispositionem stellarum: luci comparata, invenitur prior.
vulgate.7:30: Illi enim succedit nox; sapientiam autem non vincit malitia.
vulgate.8:1: Attingit ergo a fine usque ad finem fortiter, et disponit omnia suaviter.
vulgate.8:2: Hanc amavi, et exquisivi a juventute mea, et quæsivi sponsam mihi eam assumere, et amator factus sum formæ illius.
vulgate.8:3: Generositatem illius glorificat, contubernium habens Dei; sed et omnium Dominus dilexit illam.
vulgate.8:4: Doctrix enim est disciplinæ Dei, et electrix operum illius.
vulgate.8:5: Et si divitiæ appetuntur in vita, quid sapientia locupletius quæ operatur omnia?
vulgate.8:6: Si autem sensus operatur, quis horum quæ sunt magis quam illa est artifex?
vulgate.8:7: Et si justitiam quis diligit, labores hujus magnas habent virtutes: sobrietatem enim et prudentiam docet, et justitiam, et virtutem, quibus utilius nihil est in vita hominibus.
vulgate.8:8: Et si multitudinem scientiæ desiderat quis, scit præterita, et de futuris æstimat; scit versutias sermonum, et dissolutiones argumentorum; signa et monstra scit antequam fiant, et eventus temporum et sæculorum.
vulgate.8:9: Proposui ergo hanc adducere mihi ad convivendum, sciens quoniam mecum communicabit de bonis, et erit allocutio cogitationis et tædii mei.
vulgate.8:10: Habebo propter hanc claritatem ad turbas, et honorem apud seniores juvenis;
vulgate.8:11: et acutus inveniar in judicio, et in conspectu potentium admirabilis ero, et facies principum mirabuntur me:
vulgate.8:12: tacentem me sustinebunt, et loquentem me respicient, et sermocinante me plura, manus ori suo imponent.
vulgate.8:13: Præterea habebo per hanc immortalitatem, et memoriam æternam his qui post me futuri sunt relinquam.
vulgate.8:14: Disponam populos, et nationes mihi erunt subditæ:
vulgate.8:15: timebunt me audientes reges horrendi. In multitudine videbor bonus, et in bello fortis.
vulgate.8:16: Intrans in domum meam, conquiescam cum illa: non enim habet amaritudinem conversatio illius, nec tædium convictus illius, sed lætitiam et gaudium.
vulgate.8:17: Hæc cogitans apud me et commemorans in corde meo, quoniam immortalitas est in cognatione sapientiæ,
vulgate.8:18: et in amicitia illius delectatio bona, et in operibus manuum illius honestas sine defectione, et in certamine loquelæ illius sapientia, et præclaritas in communicatione sermonum ipsius: circuibam quærens, ut mihi illam assumerem.
vulgate.8:19: Puer autem eram ingeniosus, et sortitus sum animam bonam.
vulgate.8:20: Et cum essem magis bonus, veni ad corpus incoinquinatum.
vulgate.8:21: Et ut scivi quoniam aliter non possem esse continens, nisi Deus det; et hoc ipsum erat sapientiæ, scire cujus esset hoc donum: adii Dominum, et deprecatus sum illum, et dixi ex totis præcordiis meis:
vulgate.9:1: Deus patrum meorum, et Domine misericordiæ, qui fecisti omnia verbo tuo,
vulgate.9:2: et sapientia tua constituisti hominem, ut dominaretur creaturæ quæ a te facta est,
vulgate.9:3: ut disponat orbem terrarum in æquitate et justitia, et in directione cordis judicium judicet:
vulgate.9:4: da mihi sedium tuarum assistricem sapientiam, et noli me reprobare a pueris tuis:
vulgate.9:5: quoniam servus tuus sum ego, et filius ancillæ tuæ; homo infirmus, et exigui temporis, et minor ad intellectum judicii et legum.
vulgate.9:6: Nam etsi quis erit consummatus inter filios hominum, si ab illo abfuerit sapientia tua, in nihilum computabitur.
vulgate.9:7: Tu elegisti me regem populo tuo, et judicem filiorum tuorum et filiarum:
vulgate.9:8: et dixisti me ædificare templum in monte sancto tuo, et in civitate habitationis tuæ altare: similitudinem tabernaculi sancti tui quod præparasti ab initio.
vulgate.9:9: Et tecum sapientia tua, quæ novit opera tua, quæ et affuit tunc cum orbem terrarum faceres, et sciebat quid esset placitum oculis tuis, et quid directum in præceptis tuis.
vulgate.9:10: Mitte illam de cælis sanctis tuis, et a sede magnitudinis tuæ, ut mecum sit et mecum laboret, ut sciam quid acceptum sit apud te:
vulgate.9:11: scit enim illa omnia, et intelligit, et deducet me in operibus meis sobrie, et custodiet me in sua potentia.
vulgate.9:12: Et erunt accepta opera mea, et disponam populum tuum juste, et ero dignus sedium patris mei.
vulgate.9:13: Quis enim hominum poterit scire consilium Dei? aut quis poterit cogitare quid velit Deus?
vulgate.9:14: Cogitationes enim mortalium timidæ, et incertæ providentiæ nostræ;
vulgate.9:15: corpus enim quod corrumpitur aggravat animam, et terrena inhabitatio deprimit sensum multa cogitantem.
vulgate.9:16: Et difficile æstimamus quæ in terra sunt, et quæ in prospectu sunt invenimus cum labore: quæ autem in cælis sunt, quis investigabit?
vulgate.9:17: Sensum autem tuum, quis sciet, nisi tu dederis sapientiam, et miseris spiritum sanctum tuum de altissimis,
vulgate.9:18: et sic correctæ sint semitæ eorum qui sunt in terris, et quæ tibi placent didicerint homines?
vulgate.9:19: Nam per sapientiam sanati sunt quicumque placuerunt tibi, Domine, a principio.
vulgate.10:1: Hæc illum qui primus formatus est a Deo patre orbis terrarum, cum solus esset creatus, custodivit,
vulgate.10:2: et eduxit illum a delicto suo, et dedit illi virtutem continendi omnia.
vulgate.10:3: Ab hac ut recessit injustus in ira sua, per iram homicidii fraterni deperiit.
vulgate.10:4: Propter quem cum aqua deleret terram, sanavit iterum sapientia, per contemptibile lignum justum gubernans.
vulgate.10:5: Hæc et in consensu nequitiæ, cum se nationes contulissent, scivit justum, et conservavit sine querela Deo, et in filii misericordia fortem custodivit.
vulgate.10:6: Hæc justum a pereuntibus impiis liberavit fugientem, descendente igne in Pentapolim:
vulgate.10:7: quibus in testimonium nequitiæ fumigabunda constat deserta terra, et incerto tempore fructus habentes arbores: et incredibilis animæ memoria stans figmentum salis.
vulgate.10:8: Sapientiam enim prætereuntes, non tantum in hoc lapsi sunt ut ignorarent bona, sed et insipientiæ suæ reliquerunt hominibus memoriam, ut in his quæ peccaverunt nec latere potuissent.
vulgate.10:9: Sapientia autem hos qui se observant a doloribus liberavit.
vulgate.10:10: Hæc profugum iræ fratris justum deduxit per vias rectas, et ostendit illi regnum Dei, et dedit illi scientiam sanctorum; honestavit illum in laboribus, et complevit labores illius.
vulgate.10:11: In fraude circumvenientium illum affuit illi, et honestum fecit illum.
vulgate.10:12: Custodivit illum ab inimicis, et a seductoribus tutavit illum: et certamen forte dedit illi ut vinceret, et sciret quoniam omnium potentior est sapientia.
vulgate.10:13: Hæc venditum justum non dereliquit, sed a peccatoribus liberavit eum; descenditque cum illo in foveam,
vulgate.10:14: et in vinculis non dereliquit illum, donec afferret illi sceptrum regni, et potentiam adversus eos qui eum deprimebant: et mendaces ostendit qui maculaverunt illum, et dedit illi claritatem æternam.
vulgate.10:15: Hæc populum justum et semen sine querela liberavit a nationibus quæ illum deprimebant.
vulgate.10:16: Intravit in animam servi Dei, et stetit contra reges horrendos in portentis et signis.
vulgate.10:17: Et reddidit justis mercedem laborum suorum, et deduxit illos in via mirabili: et fuit illis in velamento diei, et in luce stellarum per noctem;
vulgate.10:18: transtulit illos per mare Rubrum, et transvexit illos per aquam nimiam.
vulgate.10:19: Inimicos autem illorum demersit in mare, et ab altitudine inferorum eduxit illos. Ideo justi tulerunt spolia impiorum,
vulgate.10:20: et decantaverunt, Domine, nomen sanctum tuum, et victricem manum tuam laudaverunt pariter:
vulgate.10:21: quoniam sapientia aperuit os mutorum, et linguas infantium fecit disertas.
vulgate.11:1: Direxit opera eorum in manibus prophetæ sancti.
vulgate.11:2: Iter fecerunt per deserta quæ non habitabantur, et in locis desertis fixerunt casas.
vulgate.11:3: Steterunt contra hostes, et de inimicis se vindicaverunt.
vulgate.11:4: Sitierunt, et invocaverunt te, et data est illis aqua de petra altissima, et requies sitis de lapide duro.
vulgate.11:5: Per quæ enim pœnas passi sunt inimici illorum a defectione potus sui, et in eis cum abundarent filii Israël lætati sunt:
vulgate.11:6: per hæc, cum illis deessent, bene cum illis actum est.
vulgate.11:7: Nam pro fonte quidem sempiterni fluminis, humanum sanguinem dedisti injustis.
vulgate.11:8: Qui cum minuerentur in traductione infantium occisorum, dedisti illis abundantem aquam insperate,
vulgate.11:9: ostendens per sitim quæ tunc fuit, quemadmodum tuos exaltares, et adversarios illorum necares.
vulgate.11:10: Cum enim tentati sunt, et quidem cum misericordia disciplinam accipientes, scierunt quemadmodum cum ira judicati impii tormenta paterentur.
vulgate.11:11: Hos quidem tamquam pater monens probasti; illos autem tamquam durus rex interrogans condemnasti.
vulgate.11:12: Absentes enim, et præsentes, similiter torquebantur.
vulgate.11:13: Duplex enim illos acceperat tædium et gemitus, cum memoria præteritorum.
vulgate.11:14: Cum enim audirent per sua tormenta bene secum agi, commemorati sunt Dominum, admirantes in finem exitus.
vulgate.11:15: Quem enim in expositione prava projectum deriserunt, in finem eventus mirati sunt, non similiter justis sitientes.
vulgate.11:16: Pro cogitationibus autem insensatis iniquitatis illorum, quod quidam errantes colebant mutos serpentes et bestias supervacuas, immisisti illis multitudinem mutorum animalium in vindictam;
vulgate.11:17: ut scirent quia per quæ peccat quis, per hæc et torquetur.
vulgate.11:18: Non enim impossibilis erat omnipotens manus tua, quæ creavit orbem terrarum ex materia invisa, immittere illis multitudinem ursorum, aut audaces leones,
vulgate.11:19: aut novi generis ira plenas ignotas bestias, aut vaporem ignium spirantes, aut fumi odorem proferentes, aut horrendas ab oculis scintillas emittentes;
vulgate.11:20: quarum non solum læsura poterat illos exterminare, sed et aspectus per timorem occidere.
vulgate.11:21: Sed et sine his uno spiritu poterant occidi, persecutionem passi ab ipsis factis suis, et dispersi per spiritum virtutis tuæ: sed omnia in mensura, et numero et pondere disposuisti.
vulgate.11:22: Multum enim valere, tibi soli supererat semper: et virtuti brachii tui quis resistet?
vulgate.11:23: Quoniam tamquam momentum stateræ, sic est ante te orbis terrarum, et tamquam gutta roris antelucani quæ descendit in terram.
vulgate.11:24: Sed misereris omnium, quia omnia potes; et dissimulas peccata hominum, propter pœnitentiam.
vulgate.11:25: Diligis enim omnia quæ sunt, et nihil odisti eorum quæ fecisti; nec enim odiens aliquid constituisti aut fecisti.
vulgate.11:26: Quomodo autem posset aliquid permanere, nisi tu voluisses? aut quod a te vocatum non esset conservaretur?
vulgate.11:27: Parcis autem omnibus, quoniam tua sunt, Domine, qui amas animas.
vulgate.12:1: O quam bonus et suavis est, Domine, spiritus tuus in omnibus!
vulgate.12:2: Ideoque eos qui exerrant partibus corripis, et de quibus peccant admones et alloqueris, ut relicta malitia credant in te, Domine.
vulgate.12:3: Illos enim antiquos inhabitatores terræ sanctæ tuæ, quos exhorruisti,
vulgate.12:4: quoniam odibilia opera tibi faciebant per medicamina et sacrificia injusta,
vulgate.12:5: et filiorum suorum necatores sine misericordia, et comestores viscerum hominum, et devoratores sanguinis a medio sacramento tuo,
vulgate.12:6: et auctores parentes animarum inauxiliatarum, perdere voluisti per manus parentum nostrorum:
vulgate.12:7: ut dignam perciperent peregrinationem puerorum Dei, quæ tibi omnium carior est terra.
vulgate.12:8: Sed et his tamquam hominibus pepercisti, et misisti antecessores exercitus tui vespas, ut illos paulatim exterminarent.
vulgate.12:9: Non quia impotens eras in bello subjicere impios justis, aut bestiis sævis, aut verbo duro simul exterminare:
vulgate.12:10: sed partibus judicans, dabas locum pœnitentiæ, non ignorans quoniam nequam est natio eorum, et naturalis malitia ipsorum, et quoniam non poterat mutari cogitatio illorum in perpetuum.
vulgate.12:11: Semen enim erat maledictum ab initio; nec timens aliquem, veniam dabas peccatis illorum.
vulgate.12:12: Quis enim dicet tibi: Quid fecisti? aut quis stabit contra judicium tuum? aut quis in conspectu tuo veniet vindex iniquorum hominum? aut quis tibi imputabit, si perierint nationes quas tu fecisti?
vulgate.12:13: Non enim est alius deus quam tu, cui cura est de omnibus, ut ostendas quoniam non injuste judicas judicium.
vulgate.12:14: Neque rex, neque tyrannus in conspectu tuo inquirent de his quos perdidisti.
vulgate.12:15: Cum ergo sis justus, juste omnia disponis; ipsum quoque qui non debet puniri, condemnare, exterum æstimas a tua virtute.
vulgate.12:16: Virtus enim tua justitiæ initium est, et ob hoc quod Dominus es, omnibus te parcere facis.
vulgate.12:17: Virtutem enim ostendis tu, qui non crederis esse in virtute consummatus, et horum qui te nesciunt audaciam traducis.
vulgate.12:18: Tu autem dominator virtutis, cum tranquillitate judicas, et cum magna reverentia disponis nos: subest enim tibi, cum volueris posse.
vulgate.12:19: Docuisti autem populum tuum per talia opera, quoniam oportet justum esse et humanum; et bonæ spei fecisti filios tuos, quoniam judicans das locum in peccatis pœnitentiæ.
vulgate.12:20: Si enim inimicos servorum tuorum, et debitos morti, cum tanta cruciasti attentione, dans tempus et locum per quæ possent mutari a malitia:
vulgate.12:21: cum quanta diligentia judicasti filios tuos, quorum parentibus juramenta et conventiones dedisti bonarum promissionum!
vulgate.12:22: Cum ergo das nobis disciplinam, inimicos nostros multipliciter flagellas, ut bonitatem tuam cogitemus judicantes, et cum de nobis judicatur, speremus misericordiam tuam.
vulgate.12:23: Unde et illis qui in vita sua insensate et injuste vixerunt, per hæc quæ coluerunt dedisti summa tormenta.
vulgate.12:24: Etenim in erroris via diutius erraverunt, deos æstimantes hæc quæ in animalibus sunt supervacua, infantium insensatorum more viventes.
vulgate.12:25: Propter hoc tamquam pueris insensatis judicium in derisum dedisti.
vulgate.12:26: Qui autem ludibriis et increpationibus non sunt correcti, dignum Dei judicium experti sunt.
vulgate.12:27: In quibus enim patientes indignabantur per hæc quos putabant deos, in ipsis cum exterminarentur videntes, illum quem olim negabant se nosse, verum Deum agnoverunt; propter quod et finis condemnationis eorum venit super illos.
vulgate.13:1: Vani autem sunt omnes homines in quibus non subest scientia Dei; et de his quæ videntur bona, non potuerunt intelligere eum qui est, neque operibus attendentes agnoverunt quis esset artifex:
vulgate.13:2: sed aut ignem, aut spiritum, aut citatum aërem, aut gyrum stellarum, aut nimiam aquam, aut solem et lunam, rectores orbis terrarum deos putaverunt.
vulgate.13:3: Quorum si specie delectati, deos putaverunt, sciant quanto his dominator eorum speciosior est: speciei enim generator hæc omnia constituit.
vulgate.13:4: Aut si virtutem et opera eorum mirati sunt, intelligant ab illis quoniam qui hæc fecit fortior est illis:
vulgate.13:5: a magnitudine enim speciei et creaturæ cognoscibiliter poterit creator horum videri.
vulgate.13:6: Sed tamen adhuc in his minor est querela; et hi enim fortasse errant, Deum quærentes, et volentes invenire.
vulgate.13:7: Etenim cum in operibus illius conversentur inquirunt, et persuasum habent quoniam bona sunt quæ videntur.
vulgate.13:8: Iterum autem nec his debet ignosci.
vulgate.13:9: Si enim tantum potuerunt scire ut possent æstimare sæculum, quomodo hujus Dominum non facilius invenerunt?
vulgate.13:10: Infelices autem sunt, et inter mortuos spes illorum est, qui appellaverunt deos opera manuum hominum: aurum et argentum, artis inventionem, et similitudines animalium, aut lapidem inutilem, opus manus antiquæ.
vulgate.13:11: Aut si quis artifex faber de silva lignum rectum secuerit, et hujus docte eradat omnem corticem, et arte sua usus diligenter fabricet vas utile in conversationem vitæ;
vulgate.13:12: reliquiis autem ejus operis ad præparationem escæ abutatur,
vulgate.13:13: et reliquum horum quod ad nullos usus facit, lignum curvum et vorticibus plenum sculpat diligenter per vacuitatem suam, et per scientiam suæ artis figuret illud, et assimilet illud imagini hominis,
vulgate.13:14: aut alicui ex animalibus illud comparet: perliniens rubrica, et rubicundum faciens fuco colorem illius, et omnem maculam quæ in illo est perliniens;
vulgate.13:15: et faciat ei dignam habitationem, et in pariete ponens illud, et confirmans ferro
vulgate.13:16: ne forte cadat, prospiciens illi: sciens quoniam non potest adjuvare se: imago enim est, et opus est illi adjutorium.
vulgate.13:17: Et de substantia sua, et de filiis suis, et de nuptiis votum faciens inquirit: non erubescit loqui cum illo qui sine anima est.
vulgate.13:18: Et pro sanitate quidem infirmum deprecatur, et pro vita rogat mortuum, et in adjutorium inutilem invocat.
vulgate.13:19: Et pro itinere petit ab eo qui ambulare non potest; et de acquirendo, et de operando, et de omnium rerum eventu, petit ab eo qui in omnibus est inutilis.
vulgate.14:1: Iterum alius navigare cogitans, et per feros fluctus iter facere incipiens, ligno portante se, fragilius lignum invocat.
vulgate.14:2: Illud enim cupiditas acquirendi excogitavit, et artifex sapientia fabricavit sua.
vulgate.14:3: Tua autem, Pater, providentia gubernat: quoniam dedisti et in mari viam, et inter fluctus semitam firmissimam,
vulgate.14:4: ostendens quoniam potens es ex omnibus salvare, etiam si sine arte aliquis adeat mare.
vulgate.14:5: Sed ut non essent vacua sapientiæ tuæ opera, propter hoc etiam et exiguo ligno credunt homines animas suas, et transeuntes mare per ratem liberati sunt.
vulgate.14:6: Sed et ab initio cum perirent superbi gigantes, spes orbis terrarum ad ratem confugiens, remisit sæculo semen nativitatis quæ manu tua erat gubernata.
vulgate.14:7: Benedictum est enim lignum per quod fit justitia;
vulgate.14:8: per manus autem quod fit idolum, maledictum est et ipsum, et qui fecit illud: quia ille quidem operatus est, illud autem cum esset fragile, deus cognominatus est.
vulgate.14:9: Similiter autem odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus;
vulgate.14:10: etenim quod factum est, cum illo qui fecit tormenta patietur.
vulgate.14:11: Propter hoc et in idolis nationum non erit respectus, quoniam creaturæ Dei in odium factæ sunt, et in tentationem animabus hominum, et in muscipulam pedibus insipientium.
vulgate.14:12: Initium enim fornicationis est exquisitio idolorum, et adinventio illorum corruptio vitæ est:
vulgate.14:13: neque enim erant ab initio, neque erunt in perpetuum.
vulgate.14:14: Supervacuitas enim hominum hæc advenit in orbem terrarum, et ideo brevis illorum finis est inventus.
vulgate.14:15: Acerbo enim luctu dolens pater, cito sibi rapti filii fecit imaginem; et illum qui tunc quasi homo mortuus fuerat, nunc tamquam deum colere cœpit, et constituit inter servos suos sacra et sacrificia.
vulgate.14:16: Deinde interveniente tempore, convalescente iniqua consuetudine, hic error tamquam lex custoditus est, et tyrannorum imperio colebantur figmenta.
vulgate.14:17: Et hos quos in palam homines honorare non poterant propter hoc quod longe essent, e longinquo figura eorum allata, evidentem imaginem regis quem honorare volebant fecerunt, ut illum qui aberat, tamquam præsentem colerent sua sollicitudine.
vulgate.14:18: Provexit autem ad horum culturam et hos qui ignorabant artificis eximia diligentia.
vulgate.14:19: Ille enim, volens placere illi qui se assumpsit, elaboravit arte sua ut similitudinem in melius figuraret.
vulgate.14:20: Multitudo autem hominum, abducta per speciem operis, eum qui ante tempus tamquam homo honoratus fuerat, nunc deum æstimaverunt.
vulgate.14:21: Et hæc fuit vitæ humanæ deceptio, quoniam aut affectui aut regibus deservientes homines, incommunicabile nomen lapidibus et lignis imposuerunt.
vulgate.14:22: Et non suffecerat errasse eos circa Dei scientiam, sed et in magno viventes inscientiæ bello, tot et tam magna mala pacem appellant.
vulgate.14:23: Aut enim filios suos sacrificantes, aut obscura sacrificia facientes, aut insaniæ plenas vigilias habentes,
vulgate.14:24: neque vitam, neque nuptias mundas jam custodiunt: sed alius alium per invidiam occidit, aut adulterans contristat,
vulgate.14:25: et omnia commista sunt: sanguis, homicidium, furtum et fictio, corruptio et infidelitas, turbatio et perjurium, tumultus bonorum,
vulgate.14:26: Dei immemoratio, animarum inquinatio, nativitatis immutatio, nuptiarum inconstantia, inordinatio mœchiæ et impudicitiæ.
vulgate.14:27: Infandorum enim idolorum cultura omnis mali causa est, et initium et finis.
vulgate.14:28: Aut enim dum lætantur insaniunt, aut certe vaticinantur falsa, aut vivunt injuste, aut pejerant cito.
vulgate.14:29: Dum enim confidunt in idolis quæ sine anima sunt, male jurantes noceri se non sperant.
vulgate.14:30: Utraque ergo illis evenient digne, quoniam male senserunt de Deo, attendentes idolis, et juraverunt injuste, in dolo contemnentes justitiam.
vulgate.14:31: Non enim juratorum virtus, sed peccantium pœna, perambulat semper injustorum prævaricationem.
vulgate.15:1: Tu autem, Deus noster, suavis et verus es, patiens, et in misericordia disponens omnia.
vulgate.15:2: Etenim si peccaverimus, tui sumus, scientes magnitudinem tuam; et si non peccaverimus, scimus quoniam apud te sumus computati.
vulgate.15:3: Nosse enim te, consummata justitia est; et scire justitiam et virtutem tuam, radix est immortalitatis.
vulgate.15:4: Non enim in errorem induxit nos hominum malæ artis excogitatio, nec umbra picturæ labor sine fructu, effigies sculpta per varios colores:
vulgate.15:5: cujus aspectus insensato dat concupiscentiam, et diligit mortuæ imaginis effigiem sine anima.
vulgate.15:6: Malorum amatores digni sunt qui spem habeant in talibus, et qui faciunt illos, et qui diligunt, et qui colunt.
vulgate.15:7: Sed et figulus mollem terram premens, laboriose fingit ad usus nostros unumquodque vas; et de eodem luto fingit quæ munda sunt in usum vasa, et similiter quæ his sunt contraria: horum autem vasorum quis sit usus, judex est figulus.
vulgate.15:8: Et cum labore vano deum fingit de eodem luto ille qui paulo ante de terra factus fuerat, et post pusillum reducit se unde acceptus est, repetitus animæ debitum quam habebat.
vulgate.15:9: Sed cura est illi non quia laboraturus est, nec quoniam brevis illi vita est: sed concertatur aurificibus et argentariis; sed et ærarios imitatur, et gloriam præfert, quoniam res supervacuas fingit.
vulgate.15:10: Cinis est enim cor ejus, et terra supervacua spes illius, et luto vilior vita ejus:
vulgate.15:11: quoniam ignoravit qui se finxit, et qui inspiravit illi animam quæ operatur, et qui insufflavit ei spiritum vitalem.
vulgate.15:12: Sed et æstimaverunt ludum esse vitam nostram, et conversationem vitæ compositam ad lucrum, et oportere undecumque etiam ex malo acquirere.
vulgate.15:13: Hic enim scit se super omnes delinquere, qui ex terræ materia fragilia vasa et sculptilia fingit.
vulgate.15:14: Omnes enim insipientes, et infelices supra modum animæ superbi, sunt inimici populi tui, et imperantes illi:
vulgate.15:15: quoniam omnia idola nationum deos æstimaverunt, quibus neque oculorum usus est ad videndum, neque nares ad percipiendum spiritum, neque aures ad audiendum, neque digiti manuum ad tractandum, sed et pedes eorum pigri ad ambulandum.
vulgate.15:16: Homo enim fecit illos; et qui spiritum mutuatus est, is finxit illos. Nemo enim sibi similem homo poterit deum fingere.
vulgate.15:17: Cum enim sit mortalis, mortuum fingit manibus iniquis. Melior enim est ipse his quos colit, quia ipse quidem vixit, cum esset mortalis, illi autem numquam.
vulgate.15:18: Sed et animalia miserrima colunt; insensata enim comparata his, illis sunt deteriora.
vulgate.15:19: Sed nec aspectu aliquis ex his animalibus bona potest conspicere: effugerunt autem Dei laudem et benedictionem ejus.
vulgate.16:1: Propter hæc et per his similia passi sunt digne tormenta, et per multitudinem bestiarum exterminati sunt.
vulgate.16:2: Pro quibus tormentis bene disposuisti populum tuum, quibus dedisti concupiscentiam delectamenti sui novum saporem, escam parans eis ortygometram:
vulgate.16:3: ut illi quidem, concupiscentes escam propter ea quæ illis ostensa et missa sunt, etiam a necessaria concupiscentia averterentur. Hi autem in brevi inopes facti, novam gustaverunt escam.
vulgate.16:4: Oportebat enim illis sine excusatione quidem supervenire interitum exercentibus tyrannidem; his autem tantum ostendere quemadmodum inimici eorum exterminabantur.
vulgate.16:5: Etenim cum illis supervenit sæva bestiarum ira, morsibus perversorum colubrorum exterminabantur.
vulgate.16:6: Sed non in perpetuum ira tua permansit, sed ad correptionem in brevi turbati sunt, signum habentes salutis ad commemorationem mandati legis tuæ.
vulgate.16:7: Qui enim conversus est, non per hoc quod videbat sanabatur, sed per te, omnium salvatorem.
vulgate.16:8: In hoc autem ostendisti inimicis nostris quia tu es qui liberas ab omni malo.
vulgate.16:9: Illos enim locustarum et muscarum occiderunt morsus, et non est inventa sanitas animæ illorum, quia digni erant ab hujuscemodi exterminari.
vulgate.16:10: Filios autem tuos nec draconum venenatorum vicerunt dentes: misericordia enim tua adveniens sanabat illos.
vulgate.16:11: In memoria enim sermonum tuorum examinabantur, et velociter salvabantur: ne in altam incidentes oblivionem non possent tuo uti adjutorio.
vulgate.16:12: Etenim neque herba, neque malagma sanavit eos: sed tuus, Domine, sermo, qui sanat omnia.
vulgate.16:13: Tu es enim, Domine, qui vitæ et mortis habes potestatem, et deducis ad portas mortis, et reducis.
vulgate.16:14: Homo autem occidit quidem per malitiam; et cum exierit spiritus, non revertetur, nec revocabit animam quæ recepta est.
vulgate.16:15: Sed tuam manum effugere impossibile est.
vulgate.16:16: Negantes enim te nosse impii, per fortitudinem brachii tui flagellati sunt: novis aquis, et grandinibus, et pluviis persecutionem passi, et per ignem consumpti.
vulgate.16:17: Quod enim mirabile erat, in aqua, quæ omnia extinguit, plus ignis valebat: vindex est enim orbis justorum.
vulgate.16:18: Quodam enim tempore mansuetabatur ignis, ne comburerentur quæ ad impios missa erant animalia, sed ut ipsi videntes scirent quoniam Dei judicio patiuntur persecutionem.
vulgate.16:19: Et quodam tempore in aqua supra virtutem ignis exardescebat undique, ut iniquæ terræ nationem exterminaret.
vulgate.16:20: Pro quibus angelorum esca nutrivisti populum tuum, et paratum panem de cælo præstitisti illis sine labore, omne delectamentum in se habentem, et omnis saporis suavitatem.
vulgate.16:21: Substantia enim tua dulcedinem tuam, quam in filios habes, ostendebat; et deserviens uniuscujusque voluntati, ad quod quisque volebat convertebatur.
vulgate.16:22: Nix autem et glacies sustinebant vim ignis, et non tabescebant: ut scirent quoniam fructus inimicorum exterminabat ignis ardens in grandine et pluvia coruscans;
vulgate.16:23: hic autem iterum ut nutrirentur justi, etiam suæ virtutis oblitus est.
vulgate.16:24: Creatura enim tibi factori deserviens, exardescit in tormentum adversus injustos, et lenior fit ad benefaciendum pro his qui in te confidunt.
vulgate.16:25: Propter hoc et tunc in omnia transfigurata, omnium nutrici gratiæ tuæ deserviebat, ad voluntatem eorum qui a te desiderabant:
vulgate.16:26: ut scirent filii tui quos dilexisti, Domine, quoniam non nativitatis fructus pascunt homines, sed sermo tuus hos qui in te crediderint conservat.
vulgate.16:27: Quod enim ab igne non poterat exterminari, statim ab exiguo radio solis calefactum tabescebat:
vulgate.16:28: ut notum omnibus esset quoniam oportet prævenire solem ad benedictionem tuam, et ad ortum lucis te adorare.
vulgate.16:29: Ingrati enim spes tamquam hibernalis glacies tabescet, et disperiet tamquam aqua supervacua.
vulgate.17:1: Magna sunt enim judicia tua, Domine, et inenarrabilia verba tua: propter hoc indisciplinatæ animæ erraverunt.
vulgate.17:2: Dum enim persuasum habent iniqui posse dominari nationi sanctæ, vinculis tenebrarum et longæ noctis compediti, inclusi sub tectis, fugitivi perpetuæ providentiæ jacuerunt.
vulgate.17:3: Et dum putant se latere in obscuris peccatis, tenebroso oblivionis velamento dispersi sunt, paventes horrende, et cum admiratione nimia perturbati.
vulgate.17:4: Neque enim quæ continebat illos spelunca sine timore custodiebat, quoniam sonitus descendens perturbabat illos, et personæ tristes illis apparentes pavorem illis præstabant.
vulgate.17:5: Et ignis quidem nulla vis poterat illis lumen præbere, nec siderum limpidæ flammæ illuminare poterant illam noctem horrendam.
vulgate.17:6: Apparebat autem illis subitaneus ignis, timore plenus; et timore perculsi illius quæ non videbatur faciei, æstimabant deteriora esse quæ videbantur.
vulgate.17:7: Et magicæ artis appositi erant derisus, et sapientiæ gloriæ correptio cum contumelia.
vulgate.17:8: Illi enim qui promittebant timores et perturbationes expellere se ab anima languente, hi cum derisu pleni timore languebant.
vulgate.17:9: Nam etsi nihil illos ex monstris perturbabat, transitu animalium et serpentium sibilatione commoti, tremebundi peribant, et aërem quem nulla ratione quis effugere posset, negantes se videre.
vulgate.17:10: Cum sit enim timida nequitia, dat testimonium condemnationis: semper enim præsumit sæva, perturbata conscientia:
vulgate.17:11: nihil enim est timor nisi proditio cogitationis auxiliorum.
vulgate.17:12: Et dum ab intus minor est exspectatio, majorem computat inscientiam ejus causæ, de qua tormentum præstat.
vulgate.17:13: Illi autem qui impotentem vere noctem, et ab infimis et ab altissimis inferis supervenientem, eumdem somnum dormientes,
vulgate.17:14: aliquando monstrorum exagitabantur timore, aliquando animæ deficiebant traductione: subitaneus enim illis et insperatus timor supervenerat.
vulgate.17:15: Deinde si quisquam ex illis decidisset, custodiebatur in carcere sine ferro reclusus.
vulgate.17:16: Si enim rusticus quis erat, aut pastor, aut agri laborum operarius præoccupatus esset, ineffugibilem sustinebat necessitatem;
vulgate.17:17: una enim catena tenebrarum omnes erant colligati. Sive spiritus sibilans, aut inter spissos arborum ramos avium sonus suavis, aut vis aquæ decurrentis nimium,
vulgate.17:18: aut sonus validus præcipitatarum petrarum, aut ludentium animalium cursus invisus, aut mugientium valida bestiarum vox, aut resonans de altissimis montibus echo: deficientes faciebant illos præ timore.
vulgate.17:19: Omnis enim orbis terrarum limpido illuminabatur lumine, et non impeditis operibus continebatur.
vulgate.17:20: Solis autem illis superposita erat gravis nox, imago tenebrarum quæ superventura illis erat: ipsi ergo sibi erant graviores tenebris.
vulgate.18:1: Sanctis autem tuis maxima erat lux, et horum quidem vocem audiebant, sed figuram non videbant. Et quia non et ipsi eadem passi erant, magnificabant te;
vulgate.18:2: et qui ante læsi erant, quia non lædebantur, gratias agebant, et ut esset differentia, donum petebant.
vulgate.18:3: Propter quod ignis ardentem columnam ducem habuerunt ignotæ viæ, et solem sine læsura boni hospitii præstitisti.
vulgate.18:4: Digni quidem illi carere luce, et pati carcerem tenebrarum, qui inclusos custodiebant filios tuos, per quos incipiebat incorruptum legis lumen sæculo dari.
vulgate.18:5: Cum cogitarent justorum occidere infantes, et uno exposito filio et liberato, in traductionem illorum, multitudinem filiorum abstulisti, et pariter illos perdidisti in aqua valida.
vulgate.18:6: Illa enim nox ante cognita est a patribus nostris, ut vere scientes quibus juramentis crediderunt, animæquiores essent.
vulgate.18:7: Suscepta est autem a populo tuo sanitas quidem justorum, injustorum autem exterminatio.
vulgate.18:8: Sicut enim læsisti adversarios, sic et nos provocans magnificasti.
vulgate.18:9: Absconse enim sacrificabant justi pueri bonorum, et justitiæ legem in concordia disposuerunt; similiter et bona et mala recepturos justos, patrum jam decantantes laudes.
vulgate.18:10: Resonabat autem inconveniens inimicorum vox, et flebilis audiebatur planctus ploratorum infantium.
vulgate.18:11: Simili autem pœna servus cum domino afflictus est, et popularis homo regi similia passus.
vulgate.18:12: Similiter ergo omnes, uno nomine mortis, mortuos habebant innumerabiles: nec enim ad sepeliendum vivi sufficiebant, quoniam uno momento quæ erat præclarior natio illorum exterminata est.
vulgate.18:13: De omnibus enim non credentes, propter veneficia; tunc vero primum cum fuit exterminium primogenitorum, spoponderunt populum Dei esse.
vulgate.18:14: Cum enim quietum silentium contineret omnia, et nox in suo cursu medium iter haberet,
vulgate.18:15: omnipotens sermo tuus de cælo, a regalibus sedibus, durus debellator in mediam exterminii terram prosilivit,
vulgate.18:16: gladius acutus insimulatum imperium tuum portans: et stans, replevit omnia morte, et usque ad cælum attingebat stans in terra.
vulgate.18:17: Tunc continuo visus somniorum malorum turbaverunt illos, et timores supervenerunt insperati.
vulgate.18:18: Et alius alibi projectus semivivus, propter quam moriebatur causam demonstrabat mortis.
vulgate.18:19: Visiones enim quæ illos turbaverunt hæc præmonebant, ne inscii quare mala patiebantur perirent.
vulgate.18:20: Tetigit autem tunc et justos tentatio mortis, et commotio in eremo facta est multitudinis: sed non diu permansit ira tua.
vulgate.18:21: Prosperans enim homo sine querela deprecari pro populis, proferens servitutis suæ scutum, orationem et per incensum deprecationem allegans, restitit iræ, et finem imposuit necessitati, ostendens quoniam tuus est famulus.
vulgate.18:22: Vicit autem turbas non in virtute corporis, nec armaturæ potentia: sed verbo illum qui se vexabat subjecit, juramenta parentum et testamentum commemorans.
vulgate.18:23: Cum enim jam acervatim cecidissent super alterutrum mortui, interstitit, et amputavit impetum, et divisit illam quæ ad vivos ducebat viam.
vulgate.18:24: In veste enim poderis quam habebat, totus erat orbis terrarum; et parentum magnalia in quatuor ordinibus lapidum erant sculpta, et magnificentia tua in diademate capitis illius sculpta erat.
vulgate.18:25: His autem cessit qui exterminabat, et hæc extimuit: erat enim sola tentatio iræ sufficiens.
vulgate.19:1: Impiis autem usque in novissimum sine misericordia ira supervenit. Præsciebat enim et futura illorum:
vulgate.19:2: quoniam cum ipsi permisissent ut se educerent, et cum magna sollicitudine præmisissent illos, consequebantur illos, pœnitentia acti.
vulgate.19:3: Adhuc enim inter manus habentes luctum, et deplorantes ad monumenta mortuorum, aliam sibi assumpserunt cogitationem inscientiæ, et quos rogantes projecerant, hos tamquam fugitivos persequebantur.
vulgate.19:4: Ducebat enim illos ad hunc finem digna necessitas; et horum quæ acciderant commemorationem amittebant, ut quæ deerant tormentis repleret punitio:
vulgate.19:5: et populus quidem tuus mirabiliter transiret, illi autem novam mortem invenirent.
vulgate.19:6: Omnis enim creatura ad suum genus ab initio refigurabatur, deserviens tuis præceptis, ut pueri tui custodirentur illæsi.
vulgate.19:7: Nam nubes castra eorum obumbrabat, et ex aqua quæ ante erat, terra arida apparuit, et in mari Rubro via sine impedimento, et campus germinans de profundo nimio:
vulgate.19:8: per quem omnis natio transivit quæ tegebatur tua manu, videntes tua mirabilia et monstra.
vulgate.19:9: Tamquam enim equi depaverunt escam, et tamquam agni exsultaverunt, magnificantes te, Domine, qui liberasti illos.
vulgate.19:10: Memores enim erant adhuc eorum quæ in incolatu illorum facta fuerant: quemadmodum pro natione animalium eduxit terra muscas, et pro piscibus eructavit fluvius multitudinem ranarum.
vulgate.19:11: Novissime autem viderunt novam creaturam avium, cum, adducti concupiscentia, postulaverunt escas epulationis.
vulgate.19:12: In allocutione enim desiderii ascendit illis de mari ortygometra: et vexationes peccatoribus supervenerunt, non sine illis quæ ante facta erant argumentis per vim fulminum: juste enim patiebantur secundum suas nequitias.
vulgate.19:13: Etenim detestabiliorem inhospitalitatem instituerunt: alii quidem ignotos non recipiebant advenas; alii autem bonos hospites in servitutem redigebant.
vulgate.19:14: Et non solum hæc, sed et alius quidam respectus illorum erat, quoniam inviti recipiebant extraneos.
vulgate.19:15: Qui autem cum lætitia receperunt hos qui eisdem usi erant justitiis, sævissimis afflixerunt doloribus.
vulgate.19:16: Percussi sunt autem cæcitate: sicut illi in foribus justi, cum subitaneis cooperti essent tenebris, unusquisque transitum ostii sui quærebat.
vulgate.19:17: In se enim elementa dum convertuntur, sicut in organo qualitatis sonus immutatur, et omnia suum sonum custodiunt: unde æstimari ex ipso visu certo potest.
vulgate.19:18: Agrestia enim in aquatica convertebantur, et quæcumque erant natantia, in terram transibant.
vulgate.19:19: Ignis in aqua valebat supra suam virtutem, et aqua extinguentis naturæ obliviscebatur.
vulgate.19:20: Flammæ e contrario corruptibilium animalium non vexaverunt carnes coambulantium, nec dissolvebant illam, quæ facile dissolvebatur sicut glacies, bonam escam. In omnibus enim magnificasti populum tuum, Domine, et honorasti, et non despexisti, in omni tempore et in omni loco assistens eis.

douay.1:1: Love justice, you that are the judges of the earth. Think of the Lord in goodness, and seek him in simplicity of heart:
douay.1:2: For he is found by them that tempt him not: and he sheweth himself to them that have faith in him.
douay.1:3: For perverse thoughts separate from God: and his power, when it is tried, reproveth the unwise:
douay.1:4: For wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul, nor dwell in a body subject to sins.
douay.1:5: For the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from the deceitful, and will withdraw himself from thoughts that are without understanding, and he shall not abide when iniquity cometh in.
douay.1:6: For the spirit of wisdom is benevolent, and will not acquit the evil speaker from his lips: for God is witness of his reins, and he is a true searcher of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.
douay.1:7: For the Spirit of the Lord hath filled the whole world: and that which containeth all things, hath knowledge of the voice.
douay.1:8: Therefore he that speaketh unjust things, cannot be hid, neither shall the chastising judgment pass him by.
douay.1:9: For inquisition shall be made into the thoughts of the ungodly, and the hearing of his words shall come to God, to the chastising of his iniquities.
douay.1:10: For the ear of jealousy heareth all things, and the tumult of murmuring shall not be hid.
douay.1:11: Keep yourselves, therefore, from murmuring, which profiteth nothing, and refrain your tongue from detraction, for an obscure speech shall not go for nought: and the mouth that belieth, killeth the soul.
douay.1:12: Seek not death in the error of your life, neither procure ye destruction by the works of your hands.
douay.1:13: For God made not death, neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living.
douay.1:14: For he created all things that they might be: and he made the nations of the earth for health: and there is no poison of destruction in them, nor kingdom of hell upon the earth.
douay.1:15: For justice is perpetual and immortal.
douay.1:16: But the wicked with works and words have called it to them: and esteeming it a friend, have fallen away and have made a covenant with it: because they are worthy to be of the part thereof.
douay.2:1: For they have said, reasoning with themselves, but not right: The time of our life is short and tedious, and in the end of a man there is no remedy, and no man hath been known to have returned from hell:
douay.2:2: For we are born of nothing, and after this we shall be as if we had not been: for the breath in our nostrils is smoke: and speech a spark to move our heart,
douay.2:3: Which being put out, our body shall be ashes, and our spirit shall be poured abroad as soft air, and our life shall pass away as the trace of a cloud, and shall be dispersed as a mist, which is driven away by the beams of the sun, and overpowered with the heat thereof:
douay.2:4: And our name in time shall be forgotten, and no man shall have any remembrance of our works.
douay.2:5: For our time is as the passing of a shadow, and there is no going back of our end: for it is fast sealed, and no man returneth:
douay.2:6: Come, therefore, and let us enjoy the good things that are present, and let us speedily use the creatures as in youth.
douay.2:7: Let us fill ourselves with costly wine, and ointments: and let not the flower of the time pass by us.
douay.2:8: Let us crown ourselves with roses, before they be withered: let no meadow escape our riot.
douay.2:9: Let none of us go without his part in luxury: let us every where leave tokens of joy: for this is our portion, and this our lot.
douay.2:10: Let us oppress the poor just man, and not spare the widow, nor honour the ancient grey hairs of the aged.
douay.2:11: But let our strength be the law of justice: for that which is feeble is found to be nothing worth.
douay.2:12: Let us, therefore, lie in wait for the just, because he is not for our turn, and he is contrary to our doings, and upbraideth us with transgressions of the law, and divulgeth against us the sins of our way of life.
douay.2:13: He boasteth that he hath the knowledge of God, and calleth himself the son of God.
douay.2:14: He is become a censurer of our thoughts.
douay.2:15: He is grievous unto us, even to behold: for his life is not like other men's, and his ways are very different.
douay.2:16: We are esteemed by him as triflers, and he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness, and he preferreth the latter end of the just, and glorieth that he hath God for his father.
douay.2:17: Let us see then if his words be true, and let us prove what shall happen to him, and we shall know what his end shall be.
douay.2:18: For if he be the true son of God, he will defend him, and will deliver him from the hands of his enemies.
douay.2:19: Let us examine him by outrages and tortures, that we may know his meekness, and try his patience.
douay.2:20: Let us condemn him to a most shameful death: for there shall be respect had unto him by his words.
douay.2:21: These things they thought, and were deceived: for their own malice blinded them.
douay.2:22: And they knew not the secrets of God, nor hoped for the wages of justice, nor esteemed the honour of holy souls.
douay.2:23: For God created man incorruptible, and to the image of his own likeness he made him.
douay.2:24: But by the envy of the devil, death came into the world:
douay.2:25: And they follow him that are of his side.
douay.3:1: But the souls of the just are in the hand of God, and the torment of death shall not touch them.
douay.3:2: In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure was taken for misery:
douay.3:3: And their going away from us, for utter destruction: but they are in peace.
douay.3:4: And though in the sight of men they suffered torments, their hope is full of immortality.
douay.3:5: Afflicted in few things, in many they shall be well rewarded: because God hath tried them, and found them worthy of himself.
douay.3:6: As gold in the furnace, he hath proved them, and as a victim of a holocaust, he hath received them, and in time there shall be respect had to them.
douay.3:7: The just shall shine, and shall run to and fro like sparks among the reeds.
douay.3:8: They shall judge nations, and rule over people, and their Lord shall reign for ever.
douay.3:9: They that trust in him shall understand the truth: and they that are faithful in love, shall rest in him: for grace and peace are to his elect.
douay.3:10: But the wicked shall be punished according to their own devices: who have neglected the just, and have revolted from the Lord.
douay.3:11: For he that rejecteth wisdom, and discipline, is unhappy: and their hope is vain, and their labours without fruit, and their works unprofitable.
douay.3:12: Their wives are foolish, and their children wicked.
douay.3:13: Their offspring is cursed, for happy is the barren: and the undefiled, that hath not known bed in sin, she shall have fruit in the visitation of holy souls.
douay.3:14: And the eunuch, that hath not wrought iniquity with his hands, nor thought wicked things against God for the precious gift of faith shall be given to him, and a most acceptable lot in the temple of God.
douay.3:15: For the fruit of good labours is glorious, and the root of wisdom never faileth.
douay.3:16: But the children of adulterers shall not come to perfection, and the seed of the unlawful bed shall be rooted out.
douay.3:17: And if they live long, they shall be nothing regarded, and their last old age shall be without honour.
douay.3:18: And if they die quickly, they shall have no hope, nor speech of comfort in the day of trial.
douay.3:19: For dreadful are the ends of a wicked race.
douay.4:1: How beautiful is the chaste generation with glory: for the memory thereof is immortal: because it is known both with God and with men.
douay.4:2: When it is present, they imitate it: and they desire it, when it hath withdrawn itself, and it triumpheth crowned for ever, winning the reward of undefiled conflicts.
douay.4:3: But the multiplied brood of the wicked shall not thrive, and bastard slips shall not take deep root, nor any fast foundation.
douay.4:4: And if they flourish in branches for a time, yet standing not fast, they shall be shaken with the wind, and through the force of winds they shall be rooted out.
douay.4:5: For the branches not being perfect, shall be broken, and their fruits shall be unprofitable, and sour to eat, and fit for nothing.
douay.4:6: For the children that are born of unlawful beds, are witnesses of wickedness against their parents in their trial.
douay.4:7: But the just man, if he be prevented with death, shall be in rest.
douay.4:8: For venerable old age is not that of long time, nor counted by the number of years: but the understanding of a man is grey hairs.
douay.4:9: And a spotless life is old age.
douay.4:10: He pleased God, and was beloved, and living among sinners, he was translated.
douay.4:11: He was taken away, lest wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul.
douay.4:12: For the bewitching of vanity obscureth good things, and the wandering of concupiscence overturneth the innocent mind.
douay.4:13: Being made perfect in a short space, he fulfilled a long time.
douay.4:14: For his soul pleased God: therefore he hastened to bring him out of the midst of iniquities: but the people see this, and understand not, nor lay up such things in their hearts:
douay.4:15: That the grace of God, and his mercy is with his saints, and that he hath respect to his chosen.
douay.4:16: But the just that is dead, condemneth the wicked that are living, and youth soon ended, the long life of the unjust.
douay.4:17: For they shall see the end of the wise man, and it shall not understand what God hath designed for him, and why the Lord hath set him in safety.
douay.4:18: They shall see him, and shall despise him: but the Lord shall laugh them to scorn.
douay.4:19: And they shall fall after this without honour, and be a reproach among the dead for ever: for he shall burst them puffed up and speechless, and shall shake them from the foundations, and they shall be utterly laid waste: they shall be in sorrow, and their memory shall perish.
douay.4:20: They shall come with fear at the thought of their sins, and their iniquities shall stand against them to convict them.
douay.5:1: Then shall the just stand with great constancy against those that have afflicted them, and taken away their labours.
douay.5:2: These seeing it, shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the suddenness of their unexpected salvation,
douay.5:3: Saying within themselves, repenting, and groaning for anguish of spirit: These are they, whom we had sometime in derision, and for a parable of reproach.
douay.5:4: We fools esteemed their life madness, and their end without honour.
douay.5:5: Behold, how they are numbered among the children of God, and their lot is among the saints.
douay.5:6: Therefore we have erred from the way of truth, and the light of justice hath not shined unto us, and the sun of understanding hath not risen upon us.
douay.5:7: We wearied ourselves in the way of iniquity and destruction, and have walked through hard ways, but the way of the Lord we have not known.
douay.5:8: What hath pride profited us? or what advantage hath the boasting of riches brought us?
douay.5:9: All those things are passed away like a shadow, and like a post that runneth on,
douay.5:10: And as a ship, that passeth through the waves: whereof when it is gone by, the trace cannot be found. nor the path of its keel in the waters:
douay.5:11: Or as when a bird flieth through the air, of the passage of which no mark can be found, but only the sound of the wings beating the light air, and parting it by the force of her flight: she moved her wings, and hath flown through, and there is no mark found afterwards of her way:
douay.5:12: Or as when an arrow is shot at a mark, the divided air quickly cometh together again, so that the passage thereof is not known:
douay.5:13: So we also being born, forthwith ceased to be: and have been able to shew no mark of virtue: but are consumed in our wickedness.
douay.5:14: Such things as these the sinners said in hell:
douay.5:15: For the hope of the wicked is as dust, which is blown away with the wind, and as a thin froth which is dispersed by the storm: and a smoke that is scattered abroad by the wind: and as the remembrance of a guest of one day that passeth by.
douay.5:16: But the just shall live for evermore: and their reward is with the Lord, and the care of them with the most High.
douay.5:17: Therefore shall they receive a kingdom of glory, and a crown of beauty at the hand of the Lord: for with his right hand he will cover them, and with his holy arm he will defend them.
douay.5:18: And his zeal will take armour, and he will arm the creature for the revenge of his enemies.
douay.5:19: He will put on justice as a breastplate, and will take true judgment instead of a helmet:
douay.5:20: He will take equity for an invincible shield:
douay.5:21: And he will sharpen his severe wrath for a spear, and the whole world shall fight with him against the unwise.
douay.5:22: Then shafts of lightning shall go directly from the clouds, as from a bow well bent, they shall be shot out, and shall fly to the mark.
douay.5:23: And thick hail shall be cast upon them from the stone casting wrath: the water of the sea shall rage against them, and the rivers shall run together in a terrible manner.
douay.5:24: A mighty wind shall stand up against them, and as a whirlwind shall divide them: and their iniquity shall bring all the earth to a desert, and wickedness shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty.
douay.6:1: Wisdom is better than strength: and a wise man is better than a strong man.
douay.6:2: Hear, therefore, ye kings, and understand, learn ye that are judges of the ends of the earth.
douay.6:3: Give ear, you that rule the people, and that please yourselves in multitudes of nations:
douay.6:4: For power is given you by the Lord, and strength by the most High, who will examine your works: and search out your thoughts:
douay.6:5: Because being ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged rightly, nor kept the law of justice, nor walked according to the will of God.
douay.6:6: Horribly and speedily will he appear to you: for a most severe judgment shall be for them that bear rule.
douay.6:7: For to him that is little, mercy is granted: but the mighty shall be mightily tormented.
douay.6:8: For God will not except any man's person, neither will he stand in awe of any man's greatness: for he made the little and the great, and he hath equally care of all.
douay.6:9: But a greater punishment is ready for the more mighty.
douay.6:10: To you, therefore, O kings, are these my words, that you may learn wisdom, and not fall from it.
douay.6:11: For they that have kept just things justly, shall be justified: and they that have learned these things, shall find what to answer.
douay.6:12: Covet ye, therefore, my words, and love them, and you shall have instruction.
douay.6:13: Wisdom is glorious, and never fadeth away, and is easily seen by them that love her, and is found by them that seek her.
douay.6:14: She preventeth them that covet her, so that she first sheweth herself unto them.
douay.6:15: He that awaketh early to seek her, shall not labour: for he shall find her sitting at his door.
douay.6:16: To think, therefore, upon her, is perfect understanding: and he that watcheth for her, shall quickly be secure.
douay.6:17: For she goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, and she sheweth herself to them cheerfully in the ways, and meeteth them with all providence.
douay.6:18: For the beginning of her is the most true desire of discipline.
douay.6:19: And the care of discipline is love: and love is the keeping of her laws: and the keeping of her laws is the firm foundation of incorruption:
douay.6:20: And incorruption bringeth near to God.
douay.6:21: Therefore the desire of wisdom bringeth to the everlasting kingdom.
douay.6:22: If then your delight be in thrones, and sceptres, O ye kings of the people, love wisdom, that you may reign for ever.
douay.6:23: Love the light of wisdom, all ye that bear rule over peoples.
douay.6:24: Now what wisdom is, and what was her origin, I will declare: and I will not hide from you the mysteries of God, but will seek her out from the beginning of her birth, and bring the knowledge of her to light, and will not pass over the truth:
douay.6:25: Neither will I go with consuming envy: for such a man shall not be partaker of wisdom.
douay.6:26: Now the multitude of the wise is the welfare of the whole world: and a wise king is the upholding of the people.
douay.6:27: Receive, therefore, instruction by my words, and it shall be profitable to you.
douay.7:1: I myself am a mortal man, like all others, and of the race of him, that was first made of the earth, and in the womb of my mother I was fashioned to be flesh.
douay.7:2: In the time of ten months I was compacted in blood, of the seed of man, and the pleasure of sleep concurring.
douay.7:3: And being born, I drew in the common air, and fell upon the earth, that is made alike, and the first voice which I uttered was crying, as all others do.
douay.7:4: I was nursed in swaddling clothes, and with great cares.
douay.7:5: For none of the kings had any other beginning of birth.
douay.7:6: For all men have one entrance into life, and the like going out.
douay.7:7: Wherefore I wished, and understanding was given me: and I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came upon me:
douay.7:8: And I preferred her before kingdoms and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.
douay.7:9: Neither did I compare unto her any precious stone: for all gold, in comparison of her, is as a little sand; and silver, in respect to her, shall be counted as clay.
douay.7:10: I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for her light cannot be put out.
douay.7:11: Now all good things came to me together with her, and innumerable riches through her hands,
douay.7:12: And I rejoiced in all these: for this wisdom went before me, and I knew not that she was the mother of them all.
douay.7:13: Which I have learned without guile, and communicate without envy, and her riches I hide not.
douay.7:14: For she is an infinite treasure to men: which they that use, become the friends of God, being commended for the gifts of discipline.
douay.7:15: And God hath given to me to speak as I would, and to conceive thoughts worthy of those things that are given me: because he is the guide of wisdom, and the director of the wise:
douay.7:16: For in his hand are both we, and our words, and all wisdom, and the knowledge and skill of works.
douay.7:17: For he hath given me the true knowledge of the things that are: to know the disposition of the whole world, and the virtues of the elements,
douay.7:18: The beginning, and ending, and midst of the times, the alterations of their courses, and the changes of seasons,
douay.7:19: The revolutions of the year, and the dispositions of the stars,
douay.7:20: The natures of living creatures, and rage of wild beasts, the force of winds, and reasonings of men, the diversities of plants, and the virtues of roots,
douay.7:21: And all such things as are hid, and not foreseen, I have learned: for wisdom, which is the worker of all things, taught me.
douay.7:22: For in her is the spirit of understanding; holy, one, manifold, subtile, eloquent, active, undefiled, sure, sweet, loving that which is good, quick, which nothing hindereth, beneficent,
douay.7:23: Gentle, kind, steadfast, assured, secure, having all power, overseeing all things, and containing all spirits: intelligible, pure, subtile:
douay.7:24: For wisdom is more active than all active things; and reacheth everywhere, by reason of her purity.
douay.7:25: For she is a vapour of the power of God, and a certain pure emmanation of the glory of the Almighty God: and therefore no defiled thing cometh into her.
douay.7:26: For she is the brightness of eternal light, and the unspotted mirror of God's majesty, and the image of his goodness.
douay.7:27: And being but one, she can do all things: and remaining in herself the same, she reneweth all things, and through nations conveyeth herself into holy souls, she maketh the friends of God and prophets.
douay.7:28: For God loveth none but him that dwelleth with wisdom.
douay.7:29: For she is more beautiful than the sun, and above all the order of the stars: being compared with the light, she is found before it.
douay.7:30: For after this cometh night, but no evil can overcome wisdom.
douay.8:1: She reacheth, therefore, from end to end mightily, and ordereth all things sweetly.
douay.8:2: Her have I loved, and have sought her out from my youth, and have desired to take for my spouse, and I became a lover of her beauty.
douay.8:3: She glorifieth her nobility by being conversant with God: yea, and the Lord of all things hath loved her.
douay.8:4: For it is she that teacheth the knowledge of God and is the chooser of his works.
douay.8:5: And if riches be desired in life, what is richer than wisdom, which maketh all things?
douay.8:6: And if sense do work: who is a more artful worker than she of those things that are?
douay.8:7: And if a man love justice: her labours have great virtues: for she teacheth temperance, and prudence, and justice, and fortitude, which are such things as men can have nothing more profitable in life.
douay.8:8: And if a man desire much knowledge: she knoweth things past, and judgeth of things to come: she knoweth the subtilties of speeches, and the solutions of arguments: she knoweth signs and wonders before they be done, and the events of times and ages.
douay.8:9: I purposed, therefore, to take her to me to live with me: knowing that she will communicate to me of her good things, and will be a comfort in my cares and grief.
douay.8:10: For her sake I shall have glory among the multitude, and honour with the ancients, though I be young:
douay.8:11: And I shall be found of a quick conceit in judgment, and shall be admired in the sight of the mighty, and the faces of princes shall wonder at me.
douay.8:12: They shall wait for me when I hold my peace, and they shall look upon me when I speak; and if I talk much, they shall lay their hands on their mouth.
douay.8:13: Moreover, by the means of her I shall have immortality: and shall leave behind me an everlasting memory to them that come after me.
douay.8:14: I shall set the people in order: and nations shall be subject to me.
douay.8:15: Terrible kings hearing, shall be afraid of me: among the multitude I shall be found good, and valiant in war.
douay.8:16: When I go into my house, I shall repose myself with her: for her conversation hath no bitterness, nor her company any tediousness, but joy and gladness.
douay.8:17: Thinking these things with myself, and pondering them in my heart, that to be allied to wisdom is immortality,
douay.8:18: And that there is great delight in her friendship, and inexhaustible riches in the works of her hands, and in the exercise of conference with her, wisdom, and glory in the communication of her words: I went about seeking, that I might take her to myself.
douay.8:19: And I was a witty child, and had received a good soul.
douay.8:20: And whereas I was more good, I came to a body undefiled.
